data.outcome_summary: The OECD Survey of Adult Skills 2023 country note for Austria reports descriptive proficiency outcomes for adults aged 16–65 based on a household survey with an exclusively digital assessment on tablets. Austria participated in 2022–23 (second participation; first in 2011–12) and 4,565 adults participated, with results presented as mean performance on 500-point scales for literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving, alongside proficiency-level distributions (e.g., shares at Level 1 or below and at Levels 4–5). The note also reports subgroup differences by age (e.g., lower proficiency among 55–65 vs 25–34) and by educational attainment, gender, and immigrant background, and links higher numeracy to better labour-force participation and higher wages, even after accounting for socio-demographic characteristics. It further describes trends over the decade, including a decline in average literacy largely attributed to changes in population composition.
